page.summary: Use hook distance, a real drop route or a standing pallet to contest your own carry; nearby hooks and slugging can remove the escape window.

verdict.recommendation: Treat this as self-preservation at favorable geometry, not a reliable way to escape every pickup.
verdict.soloQ: Read nearby hooks and upright pallets before taking a risky down; do not expect a teammate to create the route for you.
verdict.coordinatedSwf: Tell teammates when the Killer is carrying toward a long route or when you are being left down, so they can choose pressure or recovery without blindly following.
verdict.mainWeakness: A close hook, route that avoids a drop or pallet, or deliberate slugging can deny the payoff.

options.whyItsHere: Makes your wiggle effects stronger while carried and hides nearby hook auras; a Killer fall adds progress, so terrain and carry route matter.
Recovery while downed banks some wiggle progress before pickup; it helps only if the Killer leaves time to recover.
Shows upright pallets while downed and can convert enough carried wiggle progress into a self-release at a nearby standing pallet.
If the Killer puts you in the Dying State and leaves you there, faster recovery and one self-recovery answer the slugging counter instead of improving the carry itself.

opening: Before committing to a risky position, identify the nearest usable hook, any actual fall on the likely carry route and an upright pallet you could reach while carried. These are separate opportunities, not a guaranteed combo.

rows.situation: The Killer picks you up where the practical hook route is long or crosses a fall.
rows.action: Wiggle through the real carry; use any fall-induced progress without assuming the Killer must take that route.
rows.why: Boil Over helps only during a carry, and the Killer can choose a closer hook or avoid the drop.

rows.situation: You are left down long enough to recover before the Killer returns.
rows.action: Build recovery to bank wiggle progress, then reassess the actual pickup route rather than assuming a pallet escape is available.
rows.why: Flip-Flop converts recovery into wiggle progress; it cannot help when the Killer immediately picks you up.

rows.situation: You have enough wiggle progress while carried and the Killer passes an upright pallet you can drop.
rows.action: Drop that pallet during the carry to stun and escape, then leave the area before the Killer recovers.
rows.why: Power Struggle requires both its wiggle threshold and a nearby standing pallet; knowing a pallet exists is not enough.

rows.situation: The Killer refuses to carry and leaves you down after putting you in the Dying State.
rows.action: Use the recovery window if safe; after the one full self-recovery is spent, stop planning around a second one.
rows.why: Unbreakable answers a slug, not a short hook route, and its full self-recovery is once per Trial.

rows.situation: A nearby hook is uncontested, the Killer avoids the fall or pallet, or you are picked up before recovery gains value.
rows.action: Stop treating the denial package as an active escape plan; wiggle normally, then play the resulting hook or recovery state.
rows.why: The source identifies smart pathing, nearby hooks and slugging as direct counters.

abortWhen: No relevant fall or standing pallet intersects the actual carry and the Killer has a nearby hook.
The Killer slugs you and your usable recovery window or one full self-recovery has already been spent.

weaknesses: Carry denial depends on local hook geometry, the Killer's route and time left down; several committed perk slots can produce no escape.
killerCounterplay: The Killer can take a nearby hook, avoid drops and pallets, or leave you down instead of offering the carry interaction.
commonMistakes: Assuming Boil Over guarantees escape on any carry.
Expecting Power Struggle without both sufficient wiggle progress and a reachable upright pallet.
Treating Unbreakable as unlimited self-recovery or as a carry-speed tool.
